items.change_summary: B0005, B0013, B0050, B0051, B0052, B0064 and B0125 were rewritten: every apportioning form the panel quoted ('most of that benefit is mismatch tolerance', 'the larger part ... is distribution-shift tolerance', 'most of the effect is the latter', 'most of what it was worth ... was tolerance', the §4.1 heading) is gone from the Abstract, §3.5 closing paragraph, §4.1 and §5; the registered 'in whole or in part' wording now appears in the Abstract, §3.5, §4.1 and §5 together with the co-variation statement (mismatch and control-arm loss removed together, 8.8 to 0.8 points), and §1 states that the thesis receives no separate matched-condition verdict.

residual_gap.text: Test (a) is failed by one surviving sentence outside the listed surfaces: §4.2 (B0056, byte-identical to v3) still says a sweep without the retrained contrast 'would have attributed to the branch what belongs mostly to the training condition', which apportions the evaluation-only benefit to mismatch tolerance with 'mostly' and now contradicts §3.5's 'this paper does not apportion it'. Secondarily, §4.1's carried-over clause 'this prediction does not hold once training and evaluation are matched' reads as a matched-condition refutation of the mechanism's prediction, which sits against the same paragraph's 'the design cannot say which' and §1's 'no separate verdict'; 'was not tested' or 'has no antecedent' is what the paper's own definition licenses. §3.5's 'Most of the gap that the branch closed ... is closed by training at the operating level alone' (B0123) describes the control arm's recovery rather than a reading and is not counted, but a reader may take it the same way. The headline surfaces are clean, so what remains is a one-sentence and one-clause consistency fix.

evidence_anchor: text: §2.4 "The registered calculation started from Study 1's heart contrast as it stood before the scoring correction of Section 2.5, dz = 0.500 (about 29% power at n = 10), scaled it by the pilot's larger variance to dz ≈ 0.376, and required 58 seeds for 80% power on the Wilcoxon condition at p < 0.05. After the correction, Study 1's contrast is dz = 0.34."

text: §2.4 "That calculation covered the p-condition only. The floor condition asks for a paired difference larger than the control arm's seed-to-seed SD, which at 40 dB was 0.670 points against a paired-difference SD of 0.83 points, a standardised effect of about 0.8."
text: §2.1 "dz = 0.34 after the scoring correction of Section 2.5; the preregistration's sample-size calculation used the pre-correction estimate, Section 2.4"

text: §4.2 "it asks for a difference of about 0.8 standard deviations of the paired difference, while the sample was sized for an effect of 0.376 on the p-condition (Section 2.4), so the study was powered to detect the anticipated effect, not to confirm the rule at it"
items.change_summary: B0029 now states the registered chain (pre-correction dz 0.500 at n = 10, 29% power; scaled by the 33% larger pilot SD to 0.376; 58 seeds for 80% on the p-condition), the post-correction dz 0.34, the floor in standardised units (0.670/0.83 ≈ 0.8 SD of the paired difference) and the consequence that the rule confirms only an effect roughly twice the anticipated one; B0017 labels its 0.34 as post-correction and points to §2.4; B0055 carries the §4.2 consequence sentence. Every figure recomputes from the stated inputs: two-sided paired power at dz 0.500, n = 10 is 0.293; 0.500/1.33 = 0.376; 80% at dz 0.376 is first reached at n = 58 (0.804; 0.797 at 57), matching PREREGISTRATION_HEART.md's table; results/manuscript_numbers.json gives dz = 0.270 at 40|40, so the paired SD is 0.223/0.270 = 0.83 and the floor 0.670/0.83 = 0.81. §2.1 and §2.4 no longer report two unlabelled effect sizes. The one imprecision, that the 80% figure is a t-based calculation applied to the Wilcoxon condition, is the preregistration's own framing and the committed criterion treats the two as the same p-condition.

text: §4.4 "the heart inclusion never overlaps the lung inclusions (Section 2.3), so the spatial overlap of the cardiac-related signal with the ventilated lung that in-vivo separation must contend with was not part of the task, and the weak-component difficulty tested here is one of amplitude and reconstruction blur only"

items.change_summary: B0023 adds the inclusion centres (lungs at (±1.0, 0.1), heart at (0, 0.1), jitter ±0.05), states the disjointness with its geometric reason, names the in-vivo within-lung-field situation as absent by construction and names amplitude plus reconstruction blur as the difficulty that remains; B0062 Limitation 3 repeats the disjointness and what it excludes, naming spatial overlap specifically; B0009 fences the §1 motivation with a pointer to §2.3 while keeping the Leathard and Graf citations of the within-lung cardiac signal. tools/gen_dataset.m confirms circular in-plane inclusions (ell(c,r)), r_lung U(0.30, 0.60), r_heart U(0.15, 0.30) and ctr_jitter 0.05, which with the stated centres gives a minimum centre separation of 0.90 equal to the maximum radius sum, so the inclusions can at most touch; the centre coordinates themselves come from p2_config, which was outside the permitted files, and the code's own g.overlap element counter would let the authors state the realised overlap (0) directly. new_issues.description: The new §3.2 paragraph closes with 'the capacity control removes 0.12 points of it at most', but the direction is reversed: Table S9 gives B_wide − B ≤ 0 at every level (−0.037 to −0.124), so the capacity-controlled contrast D − B_wide exceeds the uncontrolled D − B at every level, by 0.124 points at 20 dB (2.097 against 1.973).
